newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa demand ebbs, sterling too strong.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa demand ebbs, sterling too strong.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers are shunning the cash cocoa market with sterling just short of recent peaks against the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
Cocoa price lows caused some buying of Aug/Sept raw materials last week but the industry lost interest when sterling moved higher.

Traders said the price premium for distant months created some incentive for nearby buying and cover was generally thin, but positive crop fundamentals were raising consumers' hopes of further price falls.
Investor interest in cocoa was also seen declining, which could pressurise futures.
Nominal asking prices of third quarter 1997 beans of good West African quality were at 3.01 marks/kg cif versus 3.07 marks last week and fourth quarter was at 3.04 (3.14).
Latest reported trades in fourth quarter material were done at 2.94.
The cocoa butter ratio over futures rose to 2.47 points for 1997, up three on the week.
Butter prices liquid, ex-works, were at at 7.52 marks for the third quarter and at 7.66 marks for the fourth.
Sterling was at 3.0703 marks at the Frankfurt exchange fixing on Wednesday versus 3.0010 last week.
